thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: cpu.usage spike -> multiple pods OOMKilled on cluster-west-1 (service: runtime-tokenizer)

Li (oncall): saw the page, looking now. which node pool?

Jen SRE: I can see ~6 pod restarts in the last 10m, all in runtime-tokenizer-prod namespace. Killed with OOM (CPU OOM) according to kube events.

Li (oncall): grabbing logs + top from one of the pods. ping me if you need me to page infra.

Matt - runtime: FYI I rolled up the dashboard, latency and 5xx count spiked for tokenization routes (/v1/tokenize, /v1/complete-prep).

Eva (support): Heads up — a few customers opened tickets about 500s on generation endpoints starting ~13:22 UTC. I have one ticket from AcmeCorp with a request ID.

Li (oncall): pulling pod logs...

Li (oncall): ```shell
$ kubectl -n runtime-tokenizer logs tokenizer-5b8f7 -c tokenizer
2025-06-03T13:23:10Z ERROR tokenizer: processing request id=req-9f34 cpu=98%
2025-06-03T13:23:11Z WARN  tokenizer: long tokenization loop, input_len=240000
Killed
```

Jen SRE: kube event: "container \"tokenizer\" was killed because it used more than the allowed CPU shares; Node had sustained CPU pressure". Also seeing kernel OOM messages on node: `Killed process 31245 (python) total-vm: 3.2GkB` (snippet below).

Matt - runtime: ```
$ kubectl get pods -n runtime-tokenizer
NAME                      CPU(cores)   RESTARTS   AGE
tokenizer-5b8f7           1.9          4          2d\n```

Li (oncall): top inside the pod before restart was showing tokenizer worker threads pegged at 95-100% CPU for minutes. Memory okay but CPU scheduler OOM triggered container kill (we have cpu limits set low to avoid noisy neighbors).

Jen SRE: hypothesis: tokenizer library encountering pathological input -> catastrophic backtracking in regex or BPE loop -> CPU hot loop. We saw input_len=240000 in logs which is huge.

Sam (product): Do we know which customer produced that input? Eva, any correlation with the AcmeCorp ticket?

Eva (support): Ticket includes the request id: req-9f34. I can search request logs.

Li (oncall): quick mitigation plan: 1) throttle tokenization requests at ingress by path 2) scale tokenizer deployment horizontally 3) temporarily increase CPU limit to avoid immediate OOM kills 4) identify and block pathological inputs. Starting with 2+3 to reduce alerting noise.

ops-bot: Running: `kubectl -n runtime-tokenizer scale deployment tokenizer --replicas=12` (requested by Li) :white_check_mark:

Li (oncall): patching resource limits to bump CPU request/limit on tokenizer to 1/2 cores temporarily. Applying now.

ops-bot: Applying patch: `kubectl -n runtime-tokenizer set resources deployment/tokenizer --limits=cpu=2 --requests=cpu=1` :white_check_mark:

Jen SRE: after scale + bump we see CPU usage distributed, fewer immediate OOMKills, but latency still elevated due to long-running tokenizations. We should also add a circuit breaker to reject tokenization requests with input_len > 50k.

Matt - runtime: I'll push a small env flag to tokenizer to drop requests over size threshold and return 413. Rolling config as canary to one replica.

Matt - runtime: ```yaml
# rollout snippet
- name: MAX_TOKENIZE_CHARS
  value: "50000"
```

Li (oncall): rolling that flag now to 20% of trafic.

ops-bot: Canary rollout to deployment/tokenizer (20%): :rocket:

Jen SRE: early signals: canary returned 413 for requests above threshold, backend traffic for large inputs dropped 87% on canary. Error rate improved on canary replica.

Eva (support): I've replied to AcmeCorp informing them we're investigating a CPU-related incident and asking for the exact payload if possible. They supplied a snippet — looks like they accidentally sent a concatenated log blob as the prompt.

Sam (product): ack. We should provide a post-incident note to customers who saw 500s. Also consider adding frontend validation to warn about huge payloads.

Li (oncall): Next mitigation: patch gateway to early-validate and reject > 100k chars. Also adding rate limit for tokenization route per client to curb repeat hits.

ops-bot: Applying gateway policy: `validate.body.max_length=100000` :white_check_mark:

Jen SRE: Node-level steps: two nodes showed sustained system CPU pressure and were draining pods repeatedly. I cordoned node ip-10-1-7-23 and will drain it for deeper inspection.

ops-bot: Cordon node ip-10-1-7-23: :wrench:

Li (oncall): cordon/evict done. Replaced with new node from pool, cluster autoscaler added 2 nodes.

Jen SRE: Collecting flamegraphs from tokenizer process from pre-kill snapshot (if available) and saved to s3://redwood-logs/incidents/1742501234/flamegraph.svg. Early look shows heavy time in regex_finditer in tokenization preprocessing.

Matt - runtime: I'll add a quick fix to move regex preprocessing into a throttled worker with a timeout; if it exceeds X ms we'll abort with 503. Pushing a small patch now as vpatch-174250.

Li (oncall): Once the MAX_TOKENIZE_CHARS flag was rolled to 100% and gateway validation in place, error rate dropped to baseline and pages subsided.

Matt - runtime: Patch applied, scaled down extra replicas slowly back to normal after 30m of stability.

Eva (support): AcmeCorp updated ticket: they truncated the input and confirmed requests are now succeeding. Marked as 'customer-confirmed resolution'.

Jen SRE: Summary so far — impact window ~13:22-13:55 UTC (~33min). Affected service: runtime-tokenizer, causing ~12k requests to 500/503s across multiple customers. Root cause: malformed/large payloads causing pathological tokenizer regex/loop leading to CPU hot loop and container CPU-OOM kills.

Sam (product): Please include remediation plan and follow-ups in postmortem: - permanent input validation at API gateway - tokenizer library hardening (regex rewrite) - telemetry: per-request tokenization time histograms and alerts - customer guidance on payload limits - consider offloading heavy preprocessing to dedicated workers (async).

Li (oncall): I'm going to hand this incident to Jen for postmortem and long-term fixes. Jen, taking lead for post-incident action items.

Jen SRE: Taking over. I will open a GitHub incident doc and schedule a retro. Action items I'll own: tokenizer regex audit (ETA 1 week), gateway validation enforced (ETA 3 days), add CPU time SLO for tokenization (ETA 1 week), customer communication draft (with Sam/Eva) today.

Li (oncall): Thanks team. Stand down from active paging. Leaving the thread open for any follow-ups. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged and transitioned to "postmortem" state. Incident ID INC-2025-0614-03.

Sam (product): Thanks everyone — good quick mitigation. We should also add a small note in the status page for customers who saw temporary errors.

Eva (support): Will draft customer update and coord with legal if needed.

Li (oncall): handing off fully. I put a runbook note about tokenization size limits and throttle knobs in the Runbooks repo.

Jen SRE: Closing in Slack, moving discussion to postmortem doc for follow-ups.
